title: Cultural Dimensions of Artificial Intelligence Adoption: Empirical Insights for Wave 1 from a Multinational Longitudinal Pilot Study
measurement_description: The paper evaluated human participants' self-reported perceptions of whether their religious background influences their adoption, trust, and routine use of AI tools, as part of a broader survey on cultural dimensions (including age, gender, and language) affecting human-AI interaction.
findings: The study found that religion was perceived by participants as having a comparatively limited impact on AI adoption and usage patterns. Only 25.0% of respondents agreed that religious influence plays a role in their AI use, contrasting sharply with other cultural dimensions such as language (71.4%) and age (95.2%), which were seen as highly influential.
